about: A candidate playbook for ab-run (deck@variant) and runner/ab.py --data: the guard arm with the hooks this deck was left without (DESIGN.md section 36). Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: The answers candidate: version 2 (acorns) with its attack, its two trigger rules and its holds unchanged, answer rules added in front of the engine and the engine list reordered so that the cards no rule named are no longer starved. Written from the 200 tables of bots of ab-run #27 (seed 20261260), where acorns won 47 and the stock pilot of the same deck 46: the engine rules bought 1.35 goldfish turns and nothing at the table. Why: the first play or activate rule with something to do acts, and version 2's 36-card engine list nearly always had something, so cards it did not name were left to Forge only on turns when every rule was idle. Of the games each was drawn, stock cast against acorns: Skyfisher Spider 45/50 against 22/60, Casualties of War 39/45 against 17/48, Poison-Tip Archer 40/55 against 16/56, Rootcast Apprenticeship 41/54 against 21/59, Swarmyard Massacre 45/46 against 28/45, Binding the Old Gods 27/56 against 9/51; in hand at a loss 23, 24, 24, 29, 18 and 23 times under acorns. Decree of Pain (AI:RemoveDeck:All) was cast in none of 108 games and in hand at 35 of acorns' 151 losses; on the own turns it sat there castable by land count the largest opposing board was nine creatures against our five (medians), at 16 life. Rule numbers below are this file's. Rules 3-4, Decree of Pain (destroys every creature, draws one a creature): when an opponent could kill us next turn with more power than ours (threat >= life, opp_power > power), or an opponent has eight creatures or more, more than we have, and more power. Not the wipe of a deck that is ahead. Rule 5, Swarmyard Massacre (two Squirrels, then -X/-X to every creature that is not an Insect, Rat, Spider or Squirrel, X our count of those) as soon as an opponent has three creatures: it is nearly one-sided here, and stock cast it with eight opposing creatures (median). Taken out of the engine list, where it was cast for two Squirrels into an empty board. Rule 6, Casualties of War with any opposing creature, unless our Garruk is out (its modes are chosen by Forge's AI as the spell is cast, and the planeswalker mode must not find ours). Local casts: four targets each time, all opponents'. Rules 7-8, Binding the Old Gods, and Skyfisher Spider with a token to give up, ahead of the engine when an opponent has more power than we have (Forge chooses the target of chapter I and of the Spider's trigger). Locally Binding's chapter I took an opposing commander or best creature all five times (Galadriel twice, Demon of Fate's Design, Sporemound, Great Oak Guardian); the Spider was cast twice by the first form of this rule, which counted any creature, with no token to give, and Forge declined the trigger both times (it would have had to sacrifice Hazel or a nontoken creature): hence the token condition. Rules 9-10, End-Raze Forerunners: the base's main-phase-one play and hold, at three ready attackers instead of four (it sat in hand at 11 of acorns' losses against 5 of stock's; with three ready attackers +2/+2, vigilance and trample on them is still the best use of eight mana). Rule 11, the engine list reordered: Beledros Witherbloom and Garruk first (castable only with six or seven mana, and then the best use of it: the first castable card of the list is taken, so a cheap card ahead of them used to eat the turn), then the base's engine order, with Skyfisher Spider, Poison-Tip Archer (a second Zulaport with deathtouch and reach) and Binding the Old Gods after Beastmaster Ascension; Hazel's Brewmaster and Arasta moved up behind the drain and draw pieces; Rootcast Apprenticeship added (Forge picks its modes and targets as it is cast: locally two +1/+1 counter modes on Hazel and copies of Squirrel tokens); Woe Strider and Insatiable Frugivore left near the end where the base had them. Rule 19, Plaguecrafter with a token to give up; rule 20, Cache Grab in the second main phase ahead of the mana sinks of rules 21-25 (stock cast it 48/63, acorns 36/59). Trigger rule 3: Skyfisher Spider's 'sacrifice another creature' with a token to give: Forge sacrifices its lowest-rated creature and aims the destroy; in the exam its trigger destroyed something on 13 of stock's 47 casts and 12 of acorns' 23. Left to Forge as before, and cast by it: Putrefy, Saw in Half, Tear Asunder, Windgrace's Judgment, Haywire Mite, Chittering Witch's and Garruk's abilities. Out of reach: Maelstrom Pulse, scripted as a Pump spell, which Forge's AI never casts (0 of 96 games drawn in the exam, both pilots) and a rule can cast only through Forge's own logic since it needs a target; Decree of Pain's cycling (an ability in hand). Checked at 16 local tables of bots (seeds 20263130 and 20263131; the Spider's token condition of rule 8 was added after them and has not been played). Shipped as version 3 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #36: at 200 tables of bots (seed 20261310, opponents drawn from bots-v2 under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) 56 wins against its stock pilot's 49 (+3.5 points, 95% -4 to +11, exact test 0.44) with the attack left to Forge, the better of the two attacks on these tables (the same rules won 54 with the go-wide attack). What it casts in a share of games 15 points or more below its stock pilot on the same tables, 8 cards: End-Raze Forerunners (26 of 57 games drawn against 38 of 49), Moonstone Eulogist (29 of 51 games drawn against 37 of 42), Rootcast Apprenticeship (26 of 47 games drawn against 37 of 43), Moldervine Reclamation (17 of 40 games drawn against 30 of 46), Insatiable Frugivore (30 of 57 games drawn against 42 of 56), Plaguecrafter (22 of 47 games drawn against 29 of 42), The Odd Acorn Gang (41 of 54 games drawn against 47 of 49), Wolfwillow Haven (37 of 46 games drawn against 47 of 49). It casts 10 cards that much more often (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/second-pass/squirreled-away-forgeattack-card-diff.txt). VERSION 4 (2026-11-15). Version 4 = version 3 with one rule added after the Binding the Old Gods rule: Maelstrom Pulse, aimed at an opponent's nonland permanent worth four or more (mana value, or a creature's power), the best one of the opponent that looks most dangerous (harness 0.3.4: aim; danger is life plus twice the nonland permanents). Neither pilot ever cast it at the owner's table (ab-run #42): 0 of the 60 games it was drawn under version 3, in hand at 42 of its losses; 0 of 50 under the stock pilot. Forge's script writes the card as a pump with a destroy-all behind it and its AI has no use for that. Nothing else is changed. Shipped as version 4 on 2026-11-15 from ab-run #43 (seed 20261360, the owner's table, opponents under their shipped playbooks): 32 wins of 200 against version 3's 30 on the same tables (+1.0 points, 95% -2 to +4, exact test 0.75); Maelstrom Pulse cast in 49 of the 53 games it was drawn (0 of 53 under version 3); its 49 casts went at the opponent that looked most dangerous 41 times and at the next one that had something worth four 8 times; 15 of them hit a commander and none fizzled. The rule it was read by was fixed before the run: level with or ahead of the shipped arm, and the newly named card cast in a quarter or more of the games it is drawn. VERSION 5 (2026-11-21), the candidate `v5`: version 4 with what passed its exam, part by part. HOOKS: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). SHIPPED 2026-11-21 as version 5. Every part passed its own exam beside version 4 on the same 200 tables at the owner's table (ab-run #46 to #55, seed 20261390; demo-data/ab/2026-11-21-ab-v25/, DESIGN.md section 35): wins of 200 where version 4 won 40: leader 40, aim 40, block 40, swing 43. No two parts were played together; the version is at the tables beside version 4 in ab-run #57 (seed 20261410). VERSION 6 CANDIDATE `guard` (2026-11-21). Version 5 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared and the hooks the version already has have acted, attackers are taken back when the attack leaves the seat where the opponents one after another are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that, or, when nothing kept home does, where one opponent alone is (`"guard": "table"`; a sure kill's attackers stay, and an attack stands when nothing kept home would save the seat). No cast or trigger rule is changed. VERSION 7 CANDIDATE `full` (2026-11-22). Version 6 (the guard arm of ab-run #57, which held by its rule and ships as version 6) with what this deck was left without on 2026-11-21: free damage: creatures Forge kept home attack an opponent who cannot block (`"open": true` on the attack). WHY: it was left out by a rule ("behind by more than two tables of 200") that DESIGN.md section 35 found to be close to a coin for a part worth nothing: `open` by itself beside the version before in ab-run #49 (35 against 40, 11 tables against 16, exact test 0.44); none is behind beyond noise. Since then ab-run #57 has shown the hooks acting together and the guard holding, which was written for what free damage costs; and at its table of next versions 18 of the 19 deaths by a block not made were the two decks without the block hook. No cast or trigger rule is changed. At the tables beside #57's guard arm in ab-run #60 (seed 20261410, the opponents the next versions of 2026-11-21); the rule is in CLAUDE.md, In flight.
